subject: Physics
description: What lasers are, principle of stimulated emission, types and uses, holography

options.option_text: Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation
Light Activation by Spontaneous Emission of Rays
Linear Amplification by Steady Emission of Radiation
Light Amplification by Storage of Electric Rays

questions.explanation: LASER = Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation. Predicted theoretically by Einstein (1917) — concept of stimulated emission. First built by Theodore MAIMAN (1960) using ruby crystal. Laser light has 4 special properties: COHERENT (all photons in phase), MONOCHROMATIC (single wavelength), DIRECTIONAL (very narrow beam), INTENSE (concentrated energy).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The KEY PRINCIPLE behind laser action is:

options.option_text: Spontaneous emission from excited atoms
Stimulated emission from excited atoms
Photoelectric effect from metal surface
Compton scattering from charged particle

questions.explanation: STIMULATED EMISSION (Einstein 1917): an incoming photon of right energy hits an atom in EXCITED state → atom emits an IDENTICAL photon (same frequency, phase, direction). This amplifies the light. Requires POPULATION INVERSION — more atoms in excited state than ground state (achieved by 'pumping' — optical, electrical, chemical). Distractor 1 = how lamps work (random). Distractor 3 = Einstein's photoelectric effect (different phenomenon).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: Laser light is MONOCHROMATIC. This means it is:

options.option_text: Black and white in colour only
Of a single specific wavelength
Visible to the human eye easily
Coloured like a rainbow when seen

questions.explanation: Monochromatic (Greek = 'one colour') — a SINGLE WAVELENGTH (single colour). Ordinary white light contains all wavelengths of visible spectrum (400-700 nm). Laser produces a very narrow band — e.g., He-Ne laser at 632.8 nm (red), Ar-ion at 488 nm (blue-green). This is why laser pointers are pure red/green/violet, not white. Distractor 1 — confused with B&W photo. Distractor 3 — IR + UV lasers exist too. Distractor 4 — opposite of monochromatic.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a typical use of LASERS?

options.option_text: CD/DVD/Blu-ray reading and writing
Generating raw electrical power
Eye surgery (LASIK) for vision correction
Barcode scanners at supermarket checkout

questions.explanation: Lasers are NOT a power-generation source — they CONSUME more power than they emit (efficiency typically 1-30%). Common uses: CD/DVD/Blu-ray (read pits + lands); LASIK eye surgery (reshape cornea); barcode scanners; fiber-optic communication; laser printers; surveying + range-finding (rangefinders, LIDAR); industrial cutting + welding; research (spectroscopy, cooling atoms). Indian use: ISRO uses lasers in some satellite tracking + range-finding.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: HOLOGRAPHY (3D image storage on 2D film) was made possible by which technology?

options.option_text: Ordinary white-light photography process
Coherent laser light recording the wavefront
Electron microscopy at very high resolution
X-ray imaging of internal structure layers

questions.explanation: HOLOGRAPHY — invented by Dennis GABOR (1947, Nobel 1971) in theory; made practical only after the invention of LASER. Coherent laser light splits into reference + object beams; their interference pattern is recorded on photographic plate. Re-illumination reproduces the 3D image. Used in: security on credit cards, currency notes, ID cards (Indian Rupee notes have holographic strip); art; data storage (research). Without laser's coherence, holograms can't form.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a SOLID-STATE laser commonly used in research and industry?

options.option_text: He-Ne (Helium-Neon) laser, gas form
Nd:YAG (Neodymium-doped YAG crystal)
CO₂ (Carbon dioxide) laser, gaseous
Ar-ion (Argon ion) laser, gas-tube

questions.explanation: Laser TYPES by medium: SOLID-STATE — Nd:YAG (1064 nm IR), Ruby (first laser, 694 nm red), Ti:Sapphire (tunable). GAS — He-Ne (red, classic lecture demo), CO₂ (10.6 μm IR; used for cutting, surgery — most powerful CW laser), Ar-ion (blue-green; used in shows). DIODE/SEMICONDUCTOR — laser pointers, CD/DVD readers (smallest, cheapest). DYE — tunable, biological imaging. Distractor 1, 3, 4 are all GAS lasers.

questions.stem: FIBRE-OPTIC COMMUNICATION (used for high-speed internet) relies on:

options.option_text: Reflection of laser light off mirrors only
Total internal reflection of laser pulses in fibre
Refraction of light at lens surfaces only
Diffraction of light passing through slits

questions.explanation: Fibre-optic cables — thin glass/plastic strands that carry digital data as PULSES of LASER LIGHT. Principle: TOTAL INTERNAL REFLECTION (TIR) — when light hits the core-cladding boundary at angle > critical angle, it is totally reflected (no loss to outside). This lets light travel KILOMETRES with minimal attenuation. Faster + more bandwidth than copper. Underseas cables connect continents (~99% of intercontinental data flows via fibre). India's BharatNet aims to connect 250,000+ panchayats by fibre.
